editorial.note: Unlike Romantic painters, Hague School artists had an eye for the beauty of the polder landscape.
A solitary figure seen from the back was a frequent motif in Romantic art. Here, he walks away from us, unaware of our gaze. In this way, we are both drawn into and shut out of the picture.

144801.title: Two Young Women in the Snow
144801.creator: Isaac Israels

editorial.note: An everday scene in Amsterdam in the winter: two warmly dressed factory workers or studio models. Israels painted them as if, during their break, they had briefly, hesitatingly, stopped before him. However, appearances can be deceptive.
This landscape is full of drama and contrasts. Such impressive views were very popular in the first half of the 19th century.
